fields._note: PER-COMPANY OVERRIDE of the platform default bulletFields.0, and the ONLY field overridden here - the other three still come from profiles/_platforms/workday.json. bulletFields is a per-tenant configuration of what a search card displays, not a fixed schema, and this tenant does not put the requisition id first. Measured live 2026-08-20 against the endpoint above: a posting's bullets are [employment type, district, country, requisition id, brand] - e.g. ["Regular", "Tel Aviv District", "Israel", "R0021963", "Aristocrat"]. bulletFields[0] is therefore the literal string "Regular" on EVERY posting, which is what collided the whole board into one state entry and made it permanently un-alertable. -2 rather than 3, and the difference is measured, not stylistic: the district element is ABSENT for a location that has none, so 6 of the 40 postings on this board carry only 4 bullets (["Regular", "United Kingdom", "R0020949", "Aristocrat"]) and index 3 reads the BRAND on those - "Aristocrat" on most of them, i.e. the same silent collision again, in a shape nothing would report. Counting back from the brand is correct on all 40. Every Israeli posting seen so far carries a district and would have been fine at 3; the point is that the failure mode of guessing wrong here is silence, so the index that survives the whole board is the one to use. NOT externalPath, even though it is unique on all 40: the platform note is right that it is derived from the title and changes when a title is reworded, which re-alerts an unchanged posting. It stays the fallback in fetchers/api._dedupe_ids, which is where a wrong id turns into a duplicate alert instead of into silence.

health._note: Live-verified on 2026-08-19: 3 Israel-relevant postings. expected_min_jobs=0 is a deliberately conservative floor (about 25% of what was observed), because this half of the health gate exists for slow decay over months - sudden breakage is caught by the relative-collapse check in state.py, which needs no number here. No absolute floor is set: below 12 postings a floor causes more false alarms than it catches, and a drop to zero is already covered by the total-zero check.
